clue.text: Engineered space unit, life-supporting primarily

indicators.note: engineered means put together in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is a common abbreviation for unit

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A description of a built module in orbit whose main job is keeping astronauts alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool SPACE, U (unit) and L, the first letter of 'life-supporting' ('primarily'), and rearrange them ('Engineered'). Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A space capsule is a manufactured pod that keeps its crew alive while it travels beyond Earth.

clue.text: Reporter right in centre directed around body of water

indicators.note: the word for directed goes around the water

parts.note: a pond is a small body of water

explanation.surface: Someone describing a journalist steering a boat round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Directed' reads as steering, but it means sent, as a letter is sent; the reporter here is one who files stories from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent is a journalist reporting on a subject or from a place.

clue.text: Old man drinking fruity drink recalled spicy stuff

indicators.note: the old man takes the drink inside him
called back, so the drink's letters run backwards

parts.note: kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: An old man sips a fruit cocktail and remembers something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' looks like memory, but it turns the drink round, and the old man wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a spice ground from dried red peppers.

clue.text: Free coverage for family members cancelled

indicators.note: coverage for the word refers to the outer letters that wrap round the word
cancelled says that outer covering is removed, keeping only the inside

parts.note: aunties are relatives, members of a family

explanation.surface: An insurance policy protecting relatives has been withdrawn, so the cover once free is no more.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIES with its 'coverage' (the outer A and S) 'cancelled' leaves the inside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie someone or something is to release it from knots, so the verb means set free.

clue.text: Gee up shy setter climbing above lair

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so reversed
in a down clue, this part sits on top of the next

parts.note: to shy is to throw, to lob
the setter refers to themself as ME
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: Coaxing a timid crossword setter up out of hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective for the setter, but it is the verb meaning throw. LOB ME climbs to EMBOL, then DEN goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee up is an informal British idiom for encouraging someone, making them bolder.

clue.text: Female bearing pressure on field

indicators.note: the female carries the pressure inside

explanation.surface: A woman putting pressure on in a field of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like a meadow; it is a field of work. RE for 'on' is the memo-heading 'regarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of an area of activity, as in 'her sphere of influence'.

clue.text: Shade son instead of Victor in capital

indicators.note: one letter replaces another

parts.note: V is Victor in the phonetic alphabet
capital of Austria; swap V for S

explanation.surface: A royal succession note: the son takes over from Victor in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Put S in place of the V of VIENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy yellow-brown or red-brown colour.

clue.text: Representative's greeting within Rush County

indicators.note: the first part goes inside the word for rush

parts.note: MP = Member of Parliament, a representative; 's adds S

explanation.surface: A politician waving hello while dashing round a US county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush County' looks like a place name, but Rush is a verb here. Hampshire is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampshire is an English county on the south coast.

clue.text: Rubbish dig under French road reported

indicators.note: in a down clue, the dig sits below the road
what is reported is said, so the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: rue is French for street; RHU is said the same way
a dig is a cutting remark, a barb

explanation.surface: A news item about rubbish being dug up under a French road.
explanation.walkthrough: RHUBARB is British slang for nonsense. The spelling RHU comes only from the answer; the sound is RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, rubbish talk.

clue.text: Upright engineers sited before contractor left base

indicators.note: the first pieces come ahead of the rest

parts.note: an ab is an abdominal muscle, which contracts
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Building-site talk: engineers set up before the contractor left the base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contractor' reads as a builder; here it is a muscle, which contracts. E as a base comes from maths, the base of natural logs.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright in the moral sense: someone honest has a good reputation.

clue.text: Bullets periodically hidden behind second shed

indicators.note: hidden behind says those picked letters go after the other piece

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is picked out

parts.note: the word whose alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: Spent cartridges tucked away now and then behind a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' picks the even letters of Bullets, ULT, which come 'hidden behind' MO. 'Shed' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals moult when they cast off feathers, fur or skin, which is to shed them.

clue.text: Nurse certainly stops cycling over buried valuables?

indicators.note: the word for certainly plugs the gap inside the word for nurse
the letters of OVER cycle round, last letter to the front

parts.note: OVER with the R cycled to the front

explanation.surface: A nurse on a bike halting over a buried hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests bikes; it tells you to rotate OVER into ROVE. The question mark is because not all treasure trove is buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure trove is valuables found hidden, often buried, with no known owner.

clue.text: Spain introducing low-calorie cream

indicators.note: Spain's letter comes first, introducing the rest

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
lite = low-calorie, as on food labels

explanation.surface: Spain launching a low-fat cream product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like dairy next to low-calorie; it means the best people.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream rises to the top of milk, so the cream of a group is its choicest members.

clue.text: Picture youngsters being drilled by new head

explanation.surface: A photo of children drilled on parade by a new headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a headteacher; it is a headland, CAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one kind of picture is a painting of countryside scenery.

clue.text: In a fluster after Penny delivered waffle

explanation.surface: Someone flustered after Penny brought round the waffles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waffle' looks like breakfast delivered by Penny; it is empty talk, and 'delivered' is the speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to talk on foolishly, to deliver waffle.

clue.text: Note area with lowest repositioned dryers

indicators.note: the letters of lowest are put in new positions

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A memo about moving the dryers to the lowest area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dryers' suggests machines; a tea towel dries dishes. Tea towels are dish cloths.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea towels are cloths for drying dishes, so dryers.

clue.text: A single megabyte compressed by students in Cloud

indicators.note: squeezed inside the students

parts.note: NUS = National Union of Students, the UK student body

explanation.surface: A computing note about compressing a megabyte file into cloud storage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all computing, so 'Cloud' looks like online storage; it is a weather cloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the grey, rain-bearing kind of cloud has this Latin name.

clue.text: Fixes spinning top with novel bit of string

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters run backwards
only a bit, the first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: Repairs to a spinning top using a length of string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixes' looks like repairs; here it means tight spots. 'Top' is not the toy but a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A fix is an awkward predicament, a dilemma.

clue.text: Workers maybe sip this back inside bar at centre

indicators.note: going back, the letters are read from right to left
the answer lies inside the next words

explanation.surface: Staff sipping a drink back at the bar in the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' are worker bees, and the definition is a whole phrase describing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker bees drink nectar from flowers.

clue.text: Ace struggling with hard word in party game

indicators.note: the letters are in disarray

explanation.surface: A card player finding a tricky word in a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: In the game charades, each word acted out is a charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is one mimed word or phrase in the game of charades.

clue.text: Energy stored by complex SLR cine device on arm?

indicators.note: stored by says the letter goes inside the rearranged letters
complex means intricate or tangled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written: the camera abbreviation, used as anagram fodder
E is the standard abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A photographer's tale: power kept inside a complicated still and film camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' scrambles the camera letters into SILNCER, and 'stored by' tucks the energy letter inside. The arm here is a firearm, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A silencer is a tube fitted to the muzzle of a gun to muffle the shot, so it sits on a firearm.

clue.text: Actors went ahead and performed a two-piece movement

parts.note: the cast of a play is its actors

explanation.surface: Actors striding ahead to perform a two-part dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is theatre, but the movement is chess: castling moves king and rook together.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the chess move where king and rook move in a single turn.

clue.text: Go below group almost supporting framework

parts.note: a go is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: An instruction to crawl under a band's stage rig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like a verb of movement; it is the noun, a try.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a bridge-like framework supporting cranes, signals or equipment.

clue.text: Detailed talk led by a retired acting Christian

indicators.note: led by a puts the reversed name in front of the talking word
retired means went back, so the surname is read backwards

parts.note: Christian Bale is the actor, so an acting Christian is Bale
to orate is to talk, especially pompously

explanation.surface: A lengthy speech preceded by a lapsed Christian who once worked on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: BALE 'retired' becomes ELAB, and ORATE is 'led by a' that reversed name. 'Christian' looks like a believer, but it is the actor Christian Bale's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate describes something worked out with many parts and much care, so detailed is a synonym.

clue.text: Message island blocks in advance

indicators.note: the island letter sits inside the message word, blocking it

parts.note: a post is an online message

explanation.surface: An island ordering its messages ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In advance' reads as a phrase meaning beforehand; the definition is only 'advance', in the sense of putting forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Advance in the sense of putting forward a theory for others to consider.

clue.text: Bread roll on summit?

indicators.note: roll it over, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A bread roll eaten at the top of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread roll' looks like one thing; 'roll' is the reversal instruction and 'Bread' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread.

clue.text: Exchange twisted arrow back in store

indicators.note: turned right round, so the arrow runs backwards

parts.note: a dart is a small arrow

indicators.note: the letter at the back of the next word

explanation.surface: Returning a bent arrow to the shop for an exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a shop returns counter; 'twisted' turns DART round and 'back in' takes only the last letter of store.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: swapping goods for goods or money.

clue.text: Old woman by cash register cutting overly small fruit

indicators.note: the pieces cut into the word for overly

parts.note: a till is a cash register

explanation.surface: An old woman at the till cutting up fruit that is too small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overly small' looks like one phrase; 'overly' is TOO and 'small fruit' is the definition. A tomatillo is a Mexican husk tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomatillo is a small green fruit in a papery husk, used in salsas.

clue.text: Spotted maiden clearly leaving Italy

parts.note: M = maiden, an over with no runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A young woman clearly seen as she leaves Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like 'seen'; it means covered in spots, as with measles, the original sense of measly.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly originally meant spotted with measles.

clue.text: Butcher's cut constricting with bandage

parts.note: a saddle of lamb is a butcher's joint

explanation.surface: A butcher binding a joint of meat tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: S(W)ADDLE: saddle is a joint, the back of the animal across both loins.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle is to wrap tightly in cloth, to bandage.
